name: Salamah ibn al-Akwa'
nameAr: سلمة بن عمرو بن الأكوع الأسلمي رضي الله عنه، واسم الأكوع سنان بن عبد الله
diedNote: Died in Madinah in 74 AH aged eighty (Yahya ibn Bukayr and others; al-Nawawi). A report of 64 is rejected by Mughaltay because Salamah accepted a gift from al-Hajjaj, who governed later.

deathVariants.authority: Yahya ibn Bukayr and others; Ibn Hajar, Taqrib; al-Nawawi

deathVariants.source: Ikmal Tahdhib al-Kamal 6/17 (via Shamela narrator record)

taqrib.ar: شهد بيعة الرضوان، مات سنة أربع وسبعين
taqrib.en: Was present at the pledge of al-Ridwan; died in 74.

students.name: Yazid ibn Abi Ubayd, his freed slave

companionCounts.source: al-Khazraji, Khulasat Tadhhib Tahdhib al-Kamal p. 148, and al-Nawawi, Tahdhib al-Asma' wa al-Lughat 1/229 (77 in all; 16 agreed; 5 al-Bukhari alone; 9 Muslim alone); Ibn Hajar, Hady al-Sari, fasl 10, the count for each Companion (20 in al-Bukhari, including repetitions)

flags.label: Kunya variants
flags.detail: Abu Muslim, or Abu Iyas, or Abu Amir (Taqrib; Tahdhib al-Kamal); al-Askari also gives Abu Abdullah (via Shamela).

bio: A Companion of Aslam who took the pledge of al-Ridwan at al-Hudaybiyah, pledging three times, at the front, the middle and the end of the people (al-Nawawi). He fought seven expeditions with the Prophet ﷺ, was a brave and skilled archer and is said to have outrun horses on foot; the Sahih records the Prophet's words at Dhu Qarad, "the best of our foot-soldiers is Salamah ibn al-Akwa'". He lived in Madinah, moved to al-Rabadhah after the killing of Uthman, married and had children there, and returned to Madinah a few nights before his death in 74 AH. He is the Companion of al-Bukhari's three-link chains: his freed slave Yazid ibn Abi Ubayd carried his hadith to al-Makki ibn Ibrahim and Abu Asim al-Nabil, both teachers of al-Bukhari.
